hook: Threat email names *Kacheguda*; police say it looks like a hoax
hook_b: Threat email names *Kacheguda*; police say it looks like a hoax
tldr: An email sent in the name of Lashkar-e-Taiba named Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza as targets; police ran checks and say it appears to be a hoax.

beats.what: Anti-sabotage checks were done at the named spots, visible policing was stepped up, and Cyber Crime Police are tracing the sender.
beats.why: The email threatened a 26/11-style attack and claimed at least 300 people would be killed, but gave no date.
beats.care: Expect more checks at railway stations, bus terminals and crowded places; police ask people to dial 112 for unattended objects.

event.label: Checks at Kacheguda station, Tourist Plaza

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: Update: the sender used a Europe-based VPN and a temporary email account, which has complicated tracing, The Hindu reports. No explosives were found in anti-sabotage checks.

cards.q: When police announce a likely-hoax threat, how do you feel?

qs: How often do threat emails to Hyderabad turn out to be hoaxes?
What happens to senders once traced?

facts.t: The email named *2* targets: Kacheguda Railway Station and Hotel Tourist Plaza.
The email gave *no date* for the threatened explosions.
The sender hid behind a *Europe-based VPN* and a temporary email account.

viz.verdict: A precaution; police say the email appears to be a hoax

watch: Cyber Crime teams are analysing the email's digital trail; the VPN and temporary account slow tracing.
